findings.where: First screen, the hand-written 'write to me' margin note (the page's only call to action, mailto) at desktop width
findings.fault: The page's one action is the smallest, faintest thing on the first screen. It sits by itself in the left margin, outside the column the eye reads down, and below the heading, the standfirst and the photo. Its only signs that it can be clicked are the script and a pen stroke under it, and the margin line beside it is drawn in the same way. It reads as a doodle on the pad, not as the way to contact Mark. By visual weight it ranks below the photo stand-in and the aqueduct sketch, but by task priority it should rank first.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has read the heading and wants to contact Mark looks in the column and under the standfirst, finds no action there, and is left with the nav's 'Contact'. The margin note is easy to pass over as decoration, so the visit's one job is done with difficulty.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' lecture row (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule runs right across the row under the title's underline, so 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' looks underlined and linked too. Only the title is a link. 'PDF' is the word that says what the visitor gets, and clicking it does nothing. The full-width rule also blurs whether the title's underline marks a link or is only the table edge.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the lecture clicks 'PDF' or the date, as people do on a document row, and nothing happens. Angélique will add rows like this for every PDF, so the same dead area repeats down the article list.

findings.fault: It is a button, but it is drawn as an underlined text link, the look the page keeps for links ('write to me', the lecture title). Nothing marks it as an action that replays something in place rather than a link that goes somewhere.
findings.who_objects: Someone reviewing the tile expects an underlined phrase to open another page. They hesitate before clicking it, or take the replay for navigation, and the tile then teaches the later rounds a button look that is really a link look.
